haiku-low.q1: The linked Google sub identifies the user, so they sign in. The Google email is ignored and the stored email is not changed.
haiku-low.q2: The user must enter the matched account's password on the confirmation form. If it is correct and the re-check passes, the link is inserted, then start_session runs.
haiku-low.q3: Each wrong password adds one to failed_logins with the ticket kept. At 5 failures, the account locks for 15 minutes, and the ticket and gticket cookie are deleted.
haiku-low.q4: No match: a new user is created with no password, email verified, and the Google account linked, then signed in. Unverified: redirect to /login with a message; nothing is created.
haiku-low.q5: The gauth record expired after 600 s, or was already consumed by GETDEL. Either way the state is not found, so the user sees the error page and nothing changes.
haiku-low.q6: It calls start_session: a new sessions row and sid cookie. Any existing sessions row for the browser's sid cookie is deleted first, then redirect to next or /home.
haiku-low.q7: Neither a password nor an email match is required. If the sub is linked to another user, it is refused as linked to someone else, and nothing changes.
haiku-low.q8: Redis holds gauth:{state} with the verifier, nonce, origin, next and user_id. The browser holds the state in the gstate cookie. GETDEL at the callback or the 600 s TTL removes them.
haiku-low.q9: Redis key glink:{ticket} holds google_sub, user_id and next. The browser holds the ticket id in the gticket cookie. Successful link, lockout, a failed re-check, or the 600 s TTL deletes it.
haiku-low.q10: In PostgreSQL table user_google_accounts, with user_id as primary key and google_sub unique. Database constraints enforce both rules; a unique violation is treated as refused.
haiku-low.q11: The user is redirected to the origin page: We could not complete Google sign-in. Try again or use email and password. Nothing changed. No retry; the user starts over.
haiku-low.q12: The origin field, login or settings, in the gauth record tells it. Settings stores the sid user_id at start, and the callback refuses if the current sid user differs. The link attaches to that stored user_id.

sonnet.q1: Nothing special: the account is identified by sub, not email. The sub is linked, so that user is used, the Google email is ignored, the stored email is not changed, and start_session runs.
sonnet.q2: The user must enter the matched account's password on the confirmation form (glink ticket in Redis, gticket cookie). Only a correct password (after lockout check and a final in-transaction re-check that sub is unlinked and the user has no Google account) inserts the link and calls start_session.
sonnet.q3: Each wrong password adds 1 to users.failed_logins (shared with POST /login). At 5, locked_until = now + 15 min and failed_logins resets to 0; the glink ticket and gticket cookie are deleted and 'Account temporarily locked' is shown. Before 5, a generic wrong-password message shows, the ticket is kept and its TTL is not extended.
sonnet.q4: If email_verified is true and no user matches: in one transaction a new user is created (password_hash NULL, email_verified_at now) plus the link, then start_session. If email_verified is not true: redirect to /login with 'Your Google email is not verified. Sign in with email and password.' and nothing is created.
sonnet.q5: Both cases give the error page with nothing changed: the gauth record has expired (600 s TTL) or was already consumed by GETDEL, so no record is found.
sonnet.q6: No new kind of session: it calls the existing start_session(user_id). That deletes the sessions row for the browser's existing sid cookie (if any), inserts a new sessions row, sets the sid cookie, and redirects to next (if a relative path) or /home.
sonnet.q7: Neither: no password is asked and the emails need not match. If the Google sub is already linked to another user, it is refused with a message that the Google account is linked to someone else, and nothing changes. No new session is created.
sonnet.q8: state, nonce and code_verifier (plus origin, next, user_id) are in Redis under gauth:{state} with a 600 s TTL; the state is also in the gstate cookie. GETDEL as the first Redis step of the callback removes the Redis key (and the gstate cookie is cleared); otherwise the TTL expires it.
sonnet.q9: In Redis under glink:{ticket}, holding google_sub, user_id of the matched account and next, with a 600 s TTL. The browser refers to it by the gticket cookie holding the ticket id. It is deleted on successful link, on account lockout, or when the final re-check refuses; otherwise the TTL expires it. (The gticket cookie is cleared with it.)
sonnet.q10: In the PostgreSQL table user_google_accounts (user_id, google_sub, linked_at). user_id PRIMARY KEY enforces one Google account per user; google_sub UNIQUE enforces one user per Google account. The database enforces both; code checks first, and a race unique violation is treated as refused.
sonnet.q11: The user is redirected to the origin page with 'We could not complete Google sign-in. Try again or use email and password.' Nothing changes besides gauth being consumed. There is no retry (short timeout, no retry); the user must start over.
sonnet.q12: By the origin stored in the gauth record (login or settings). For settings, user_id from the sid session is stored in gauth at start; at the callback, if the current sid user differs from the stored user_id, it shows the error page. The link is made for that user.
